content:
Students in basic education in Nuevo Laredo return to class on Tuesday, November 3, after a four-day break that ran from Friday, October 30 through Monday, November 2.

The break was confirmed by Mexico's Secretariat of Public Education (SEP) and the Tamaulipas Secretariat of Education (SET) for preschool, primary and secondary students, in public schools and schools incorporated into the SEP and SET systems.

Friday, October 30 was a suspension of classes for students because of the second regular session of the School Technical Council (Consejo Técnico Escolar), and Monday, November 2 was a general suspension of teaching and administrative work for Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead, Fieles Difuntos), an institutional holiday on the national education calendar. Classes resume as usual on the morning of Tuesday, November 3.

The extended break coincided with the city's Día de Muertos cultural activities and family movement across the border region over the weekend. For parents, the return means a normal school morning again — and, for students, the start of the run toward the end of the fall term.
